claims.text: An adhesion-promoted ultrathin ALD alumina coating followed by mild annealing will significantly enhance the molten-aluminum corrosion resistance of boride-based components.
The proposed substrates are boride-based materials such as ZrB2 or TiB2.
The alumina film is to be deposited by atomic layer deposition over an intermediate adhesion-promoting layer.
The intermediate layer will improve adhesion of the ALD alumina coating.
The coating is to be deposited at approximately 250 °C.
The coated component is to be annealed at around 600 °C in an inert atmosphere.
Annealing at around 600 °C will enhance film crystallinity.
Annealing at around 600 °C will enhance coating adhesion without compromising the boride substrate.
The treatment will produce a uniform, conformal, and adherent alumina barrier covering all surface features.
The alumina barrier will prevent direct contact between molten aluminum and the boride substrate.
Alumina acts as a chemically inert barrier to molten aluminum.
The intermediate adhesion layer will reduce the risk of coating delamination.
Reduced direct contact and delamination will reduce corrosive attack on the boride substrate.
Coated components will have significantly lower corrosion rates than uncoated boride components under identical molten-aluminum exposure.
The coated components will exhibit less mass loss than uncoated controls.
The coated components will exhibit less interfacial degradation than uncoated controls.
The corrosion-resistance improvement will persist only while the alumina film remains intact, adherent, and defect-free under service temperatures and mechanical and thermal stresses.
